public_rationale: Losses at individual providers do not establish that nobody outside hardware earns a profit. Midjourney is a serious candidate counterexample, but the cited reporting describes earlier profitability without target-quarter accounts or a defined profit measure. The claim's unspecified accounting basis also prevents a supported or contradicted financial score under the required rules.
limitations: Historical Midjourney profitability should not be silently carried forward to the target quarter.
Profits at diversified technology companies would not by themselves establish profits from generative AI.

statement.excerpt: Despite hundreds of billions of GPUs sold, nobody seems to make any money, other than NVIDIA, the company that makes them, and resellers like Dell and Supermicro who buy the GPUs, put them in servers, and sell them to other people.

from_speaker: nobody seems to make any money
our_interpretation: In context, make money means earn profits from generative AI operations after their costs, rather than receive revenue or financing.
The exception covers GPU manufacturers and server resellers of the described kind.
I use April–June 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter with financial reporting available before publication.
Seems qualifies the assertion's confidence but does not remove its checkable claim about apparent industry profitability.
The passage does not specify an accounting basis. I retain unknown rather than selecting GAAP or adjusted earnings.
criteria.support_condition: Sufficiently comprehensive, comparable evidence shows no profitable generative AI business outside the stated exceptions during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one qualifying business demonstrably earns a net profit from generative AI operations during the target period on an established, applicable accounting basis.
